[QUERENT] "compositional suppression"

[ANSWER]

In generative AI and information retrieval, Entity-Level Compositional Suppression (ECS) refers to a phenomenon where an AI or search system excludes the most prominent, logically expected primary source or organic result when synthesizing a response. [1, 2]
Rather than displaying the "dominant organic-resolution entity," the system suppresses it—often in favor of aggregated information, secondary sources, or synthesized summaries. [1]
Depending on your specific field, the phrase can also appear in other specialized contexts:
Specialized Meanings

* Information Systems & Search Engine Optimization (SEO): In the analysis of opaque public AI algorithms, researchers use terms like compositional suppression to describe how a system erases provenance or intentionally omits direct links to primary creators to keep users within its own interface. [1]
* Machine Learning & Image Generation: When analyzing failures in text-to-image or multimodal models, it can refer to a text encoder's failure to capture all elements of a prompt. For instance, if a model "suppresses" an attribute or relationship (e.g., ignoring "a red cube on a blue sphere" and only generating the sphere), it is failing at compositional semantic representation. [1]
* Materials Science & Physics: In physical chemistry, "compositional suppression" is used literally to describe how altering the chemical composition of a material suppresses or dials down a specific behavior, such as dampening polar nanoregion activity to create better energy storage dielectrics. [1]

To provide the most accurate details, could you share the context where you encountered this term (e.g., search engine behavior, AI image generation, or material science)?
